title: A two-term locally finite free resolution of an integral local system
statement: Let ℓ be prime, E a finite normed extension of Q_ℓ, X a scheme with noetherian underlying space, and P a locally finitely presented module over the ordinary integral condensed coefficient ring on X. There exist modules F1 and F0, maps f:F1→F0 and g:F0→P with f g=0, such that 0→F1→F0→P→0 is short exact, and each Fi becomes a finite free module on a pro-etale covering of X. The covers of F1 and F0 may differ. Torsion in P is allowed. These are existential witnesses used in proofs, not data defining a library object.

source.place: Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(3), local finite DVR resolution; globalization argument expanded from this step; Remark 7.3.2 and Lemma 7.3.9 for finite locally constant torsors

proof.text: Evaluate presentation matrices at geometric points. Descent makes the finite fiber module independent of the lift; flat going-down and equality of continuous functions on comparable points make its Smith invariants specialization invariant. The finitely many irreducible components and their intersections make the module type fixed on each of the finitely many connected components. Continuous pivot elimination then locally identifies P with that finite DVR module, including the zero matrix case.

Its torsion T has finite fibers and a uniform annihilator, and L=P/T is locally finite free. The sheaf of splittings of 0→T→P→L→0 is locally a torsor under the finite local system Hom(L,T). Finite local systems and their finite torsors are trivialized by finite etale covers. Choose a finite etale surjection on which T is constant and the extension splits; on that cover resolve T by finite free constant modules and add L in degree zero. Zero torsion uses the identity cover.

Push the resulting degree-zero locally finite free module down along the finite etale cover. Compose its surjection with the finite etale counit onto P, giving an epimorphism F0→P. Finite etale pushforward preserves local finite freeness, as seen on split fibers. The counit is the sum map on these fibers and is surjective without dividing by the covering degree; the argument remains integral when that degree is divisible by the residue characteristic. The kernel F1 is locally finite free by continuous Smith normal form for a surjection onto a fixed finite DVR module. Take the kernel inclusion and its canonical zero composite to obtain the short exact sequence. Empty schemes use zero modules and empty covers.
